title: Generalized covers of presheaves
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small category, in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], with a Grothendieck topology $J$: a sieve on $A$ is a collection of arrows into $A$ closed under precomposition; the maximal sieve covers, and covering sieves satisfy pullback stability and transitivity. Let $P,Q:\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathsf{Sets}$ be presheaves and $p:P\to Q$ a natural transformation. For $q\in Q(A)$ define its lifting sieve
$$R(p,q)=\{u:B\to A\mid\exists x\in P(B),\ p_B(x)=Q(u)(q)\}.$$
Call $p$ a generalized cover, or locally surjective, if $R(p,q)\in J(A)$ for every $A$ and $q$. Equivalently, writing $h_A(B)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(B,A)$, every map $h_A\to Q$ lifts to $P$ after restriction along each arrow of a covering sieve; the lifts are not required to be compatible.

source.place: Dugger--Hollander--Isaksen, Section 3, definition of generalized cover immediately after Proposition 3.3, before equation (3.4). Mathlib CategoryTheory/Sites/LocallySurjective.lean, imageSieve and IsLocallySurjective.

mathlib_match.how: Read lines 35-53 and 92-96 of the pinned Mathlib. Specialize A to Type: imageSieve (line 49) is exactly R(p,q), and IsLocallySurjective (line 94) requires that sieve to cover for every q. Evaluating a map h_A -> Q at id_A identifies it with q, so the representable formulation is the same definition.
